description: One specific tension for the wrist and hand muscles, calibrated to measured strength. Peak force = PCSA x value for every muscle listed here and in hand_intrinsic_muscles.json. Not applied to the elbow and forearm-rotation muscles (BRD, PT, PQ, SUP): they keep their earlier forces. scripts/fit_specific_tension.py fits the value and writes the forces.

holzbaur2005.citation: Holzbaur KRS, Murray WM, Delp SL. A model of the upper extremity for simulating musculoskeletal surgery and analyzing neuromuscular control. Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840, 2005.
holzbaur2005.location: Table 1 (PCSA from Lieber et al. 1990, 1992, Jacobson et al. 1992; 45 N/cm2 for forearm and hand, 140 N/cm2 proximally, attributed to disuse atrophy in the cadaver specimens, p. 833); text p. 835 (peak wrist moments of Delp et al. 1996: flexion 11, extension 6.5 N m)

lieber1992.citation: Lieber RL, Jacobson MD, Fazeli BM, Abrams RA, Botte MJ. Architecture of selected muscles of the arm and forearm: anatomy and implications for tendon transfer. J Hand Surg Am 17(5):787-798, 1992.

jacobson1992.citation: Jacobson MD, Raab R, Fazeli BM, Abrams RA, Botte MJ, Lieber RL. Architectural design of the human intrinsic hand muscles. J Hand Surg Am 17(5):804-809, 1992.

mcgee2020.citation: McGee C, Hoehn A, Hoenshell C, McIlrath S, Sterling H, Swan H. Age and gender stratified adult myometric reference values of isometric intrinsic hand strength. J Hand Ther 33(3):402-410.e2, 2020.
mcgee2020.location: Table 2 (men, dominant hand, all ages, n = 256): index MCP abduction 63.7 +- 19.7 N, index MCP flexion 72.0 +- 20.5 N, little-finger abduction 43.1 +- 13.1 N; sling at the PIP (Schreuders et al. 2006)

mathiowetz1985.citation: Mathiowetz V, Kashman N, Volland G, Weber K, Dowe M, Rogers S. Grip and pinch strength: normative data for adults. Arch Phys Med Rehabil 66:69-72, 1985.
mathiowetz1985.location: Tables 2-4, right hand, all subjects, 628 men and women: men, grip 104.3 +- 28.3 lb, tip pinch 17.0 +- 4.1 lb, key pinch 24.5 +- 4.6 lb; women 62.8 / 11.3 / 16.2 lb (checked against the tables)

ketchum1978.citation: Ketchum LD, Thompson D, Pocock G, Wallingford D. A clinical study of forces generated by the intrinsic muscles of the index finger and the extrinsic flexor and extensor muscles of the hand. J Hand Surg Am 3(6):571-578, 1978.
ketchum1978.location: As reproduced by Brand & Hollister, Clinical Mechanics of the Hand, 2nd ed. 1993, Tables 14-4 to 14-7 pp. 369-370, and wrist extension 69.6 kg cm p. 368 (flaccid fingers, n = 15)

infantolino2014.citation: Infantolino BW, Challis JH. Measuring subject specific muscle model parameters of the first dorsal interosseous in vivo. Ann Biomed Eng 42:1331-1339, 2014.
infantolino2014.location: Table 2 (FDI maximum force 93.3 N); p. 1337: in-vivo PCSA 3.6 +- 0.3 cm2 at 25 N/cm2 against 1.8 +- 0.6 cm2 in cadavers

obrien2010.citation: O'Brien TD, Reeves ND, Baltzopoulos V, Jones DA, Maganaris CN. In vivo measurements of muscle specific tension in adults and children. Exp Physiol 95(1):202-210, 2010.

brand1981.citation: Brand PW, Beach RB, Thompson DE. Relative tension and potential excursion of muscles in the forearm and hand. J Hand Surg Am 6(3):209-219, 1981.

loren1996.citation: Loren GJ, Shoemaker SD, Burkholder TJ, Jacobson MD, Friden J, Lieber RL. Human wrist motors. J Biomech 29(3):331-342, 1996.

christophy2012.citation: Christophy M, Faruk Senan NA, Lotz JC, O'Reilly OM. A musculoskeletal model for the lumbar spine. Biomech Model Mechanobiol 11:19-34, 2012.
christophy2012.location: p. 22: reported values 34-100 N/cm2, recent models 35-61 N/cm2

reference_subject.choice: adult man, right or dominant hand, mean over all ages
reference_subject.why: The model's body is an 84 kg man (de Leva 1996's male segment shares), and McGee's and Mathiowetz's all-age male means are the largest cohorts with SDs (n = 256; n = 628 men and women). O'Driscoll 1992 (402.1 +- 131.4 N) and Valero-Cuevas 2003 (51.9 +- 20.4 N) are mixed cohorts and stay as protocol checks in hand_function.json.

index_abduction.protocol: 63.7 N x PP2 length 42.6 mm; model: DI1 heads at activation 1, hand at rest

little_abduction.protocol: 43.1 N x PP5 length 36.1 mm; model: ADM and FDM at activation 1, hand at rest

grip.protocol: Jamar second position; model: McFarland protocol, self-selected wrist, 0.15 s

key_pinch.protocol: B&L pinch gauge; model: lateral pinch protocol

index_mcp_flexion.protocol: 72.0 N x 42.6 mm x 73 % (Ketchum: the extrinsics give 27 % of this moment); model: DI1, PI1, LUM1 at activation 1

wrist_extension_prime.protocol: 69.6 kg cm, flaccid fingers (Delp 1996: 6.5 N m); SD assumed 30 % as McGee's; model: peak over the wrist range, ECRL, ECRB, ECU at activation 1

wrist_flexion_prime.protocol: Delp et al. 1996 as reported; finger activity not stated, so a bracket with the next row; SD assumed 30 %; model: FCR, FCU, PL

wrist_flexion_all.protocol: as above, every wrist flexor including FDS, FDP and FPL (as Holzbaur's model counts them)

wrist_extension_all.protocol: as above, every wrist extensor including EDC, EDM, EIP, EPL

tip_pinch.note: Verified in Table 3 (17.0 / 11.3 lb); not used: the model has no tip-pinch protocol.

direct_force_checks.note: Published force estimates of single muscles. Not fitted: they ask for a third of the value that strength does.

published_range.note: Published specific tensions in the sources here
